title: Deal Patterns
description: Analyze 12 variables across closed deals to identify what predicts wins and losses, so you can replicate what works and cut what doesn't

children.text: Find the variables that predict whether a deal closes. Work from the deal data the user provides or pastes.

| # | Variable | What to Measure |
|---|----------|----------------|
| 1 | Time to first reply | How quickly did they respond to the initial offer? |
| 2 | Email open count | How many times did they open emails? |
| 3 | Price sensitivity | Did the deal close at ask price, or require drops? |
| 4 | Number of price drops | How many drops before close or loss? |
| 5 | Days in pipeline | Total time from offer to close or loss |
| 6 | Stage velocity | How long did the deal sit in each stage? |
| 7 | Product category | Which categories have the highest win rate? |
| 8 | Deal size | Do larger or smaller deals close at higher rates? |
| 9 | Inbound vs. triggered | Did they initiate, or were they reactivated? |
| 10 | Objection count | How many objections were raised? |
| 11 | Thread activity | Active exchange or one-sided communication? |
| 12 | Deadline proximity | Did timing or urgency correlate with close? |
Ask the user to provide closed-won and closed-lost deal data for the time range or segment they want to analyze. Collect as many of the 12 variables as available for each deal.
For each variable, compare averages between won and lost deals. Flag variables where the gap is significant.
Determine which 3-4 variables most clearly separate wins from losses. These are the leading indicators.

```

```
